learning_objectives: Identify the causes of the French Revolution
Describe key events of the Revolution
Explain the impact of the Revolution on modern democracy

concepts.name: Estates System
concepts.definition: French society was divided into three estates: clergy (First), nobility (Second), and commoners (Third)
concepts.explanation: The Third Estate comprised 98% of the population but had no political power, leading to resentment.

concepts.name: Storming of the Bastille
concepts.definition: On July 14, 1789, Parisians stormed the Bastille prison, marking the start of the Revolution
concepts.explanation: The Bastille symbolized royal tyranny. Its fall inspired revolutionaries across France.

concepts.name: Reign of Terror
concepts.definition: A period (1793-1794) when revolutionary leader Robespierre executed thousands of perceived enemies
concepts.explanation: The Committee of Public Safety used the guillotine to eliminate opposition, executing ~17,000 people.

definitions.definition: A forcible overthrow of a government or social order
A system of government by the whole population through elected representatives
A machine used for beheading during the French Revolution

common_misconceptions.misconception: The French Revolution was only about poverty
common_misconceptions.correct_understanding: It was driven by a combination of economic crisis, social inequality, and Enlightenment ideas
common_misconceptions.why_students_think_this: Textbooks emphasize economic hardship, but ideas of liberty were equally important

periods.title: Causes of the French Revolution
learning_objectives: Identify social, economic, and political causes

entry_ticket.question: What would make you want to change your government?

periods.teacher_script: Begin with the Three Estates system...
periods.blackboard_notes:
# Causes of French Revolution
1. Social: Estates System (inequality)
2. Economic: Bankruptcy, food shortages
3. Political: Weak leadership of Louis XVI
4. Intellectual: Enlightenment ideas

exit_ticket.question: List two causes of the French Revolution

homework.description: Read about the meeting of the Estates General
questions: Why did the Third Estate want voting by head rather than by estate?

mentor_moment.anecdote: The philosopher Rousseau wrote 'Man is born free, but everywhere he is in chains'
mentor_moment.connection_to_topic: Enlightenment ideas directly inspired revolutionary thinking

classroom_activities.title: The Estates General Debate
classroom_activities.teacher_instructions: Assign students to estates and moderate a debate about tax reform
classroom_activities.student_instructions: Argue for your estate's position on taxation
classroom_activities.success_criteria: Students can articulate the grievances of each estate

periods.title: Key Events of the Revolution

entry_ticket.question: Why do you think the revolutionaries attacked the Bastille?
entry_ticket.purpose: Lead into discussion of revolutionary symbols

periods.teacher_script: Create a timeline of key events...
periods.blackboard_notes:
# Timeline: 1789-1794
- July 14, 1789: Storming of Bastille
- Aug 1789: Declaration of Rights of Man
- Oct 1789: Women's March on Versailles
- 1793-94: Reign of Terror

exit_ticket.question: What was the Reign of Terror?
exit_ticket.expected_answer: A period when Robespierre executed perceived enemies of the revolution

homework.description: Research one event from the timeline
questions: Describe what happened and why it was significant

mentor_moment.anecdote: The guillotine was actually proposed by a doctor as a 'humane' execution method
mentor_moment.connection_to_topic: Shows how even good intentions can lead to terrible outcomes

classroom_activities.title: Was the Revolution Justified?
classroom_activities.teacher_instructions: Divide class into pro and anti-revolution groups
classroom_activities.student_instructions: Debate whether the violence of the Revolution was justified
classroom_activities.success_criteria: Students use historical evidence to support arguments

mcqs.question: What date is celebrated as the beginning of the French Revolution?
mcqs.explanation: The Storming of the Bastille on July 14 marks the beginning

mcqs.question: Which Enlightenment idea influenced the revolutionaries?
mcqs.explanation: Montesquieu's idea of separation of powers influenced the revolutionaries

short_answers.question: Explain the Estates System in pre-revolutionary France
short_answers.model_answer: French society had three estates: clergy (First), nobility (Second), and commoners (Third). The Third Estate (98% of population) had no political power but paid all taxes.
short_answers.rubric: 1 mark for naming all three estates, 1 mark for explaining inequality, 1 mark for mentioning tax burden

long_answers.question: Analyze the causes and consequences of the French Revolution. Was the Revolution ultimately successful in achieving its goals?
long_answers.model_answer: The Revolution was caused by social inequality, economic crisis, and Enlightenment ideas. It ended the monarchy, established a republic, spread nationalist ideas across Europe. In the short term it led to the Reign of Terror and Napoleon's dictatorship, but long-term it established democratic ideals that influenced revolutions worldwide.
long_answers.rubric: 2 marks for causes, 2 marks for consequences, 1 mark for critical analysis

learning_gaps.description: Students think revolution was only about poverty
learning_gaps.diagnostic_question: What role did ideas play in causing the French Revolution?
learning_gaps.expected_wrong_answer: Ideas didn't matter; it was about hunger
learning_gaps.remedial_action: Assign reading on Enlightenment philosophers and their influence
